_doc:
Tool registry for creator-led reels. ONE slot per pipeline stage. Rule: before writing any code for a stage, use the slot's `use_first`; if you must deviate, log one line in videos/

/DEVIATIONS.md and tell the user at hand-off. When the user brings a new tool: add it under `installed` with its verdict from a bake-off on the same clip, then change `order`. `check` strings: path: | env: (also looked up in ~/.config/hyperframes/secrets.env, never printed) | cmd: | engine: | none.

asr.use_first: scripts/transcribe.py (adapter: runs the engines in `order`, applies the acceptance test, logs analysis/asr_log.json)
asr.order_note: Non-English order comes from the 2026-10-04 Hinglish bake-off below. The engine's own `hyperframes transcribe` defaults to English-only whisper.cpp models; with -m large-v3 it is the same engine class as vibe-server, so expect the same Hinglish weakness. Insert the user's new engine FIRST once it beats these on the bake-off.
asr.accept: scripts/asr_coverage.py: >=97% of speech frames covered by words, no uncovered speech run > 2 s, no 'subscribe'-style ghosts

installed.name: ElevenLabs Scribe v1
installed.verdict: reference quality on Hinglish; word times; cents per clip

installed.name: openai-whisper (python) small
installed.verdict: Hindi-word recall 42% vs Scribe, 19 s missing: unusable for Hindi, fine for English

installed.name: hyperframes transcribe (whisper.cpp, optional Parakeet)
installed.verdict: not run on Hinglish; default model small.en is English-only; Parakeet via `hyperframes models install parakeet`

installed.name: vibe-server 0.6.10 + whisper large-v3 q5_0 (thewh1teagle/vibe, MIT)
installed.verdict: 2026-10-04 bake-off on the 72 s Hinglish clip: Hindi-word recall 23-24% vs Scribe (0% with auto-language), 4-6 'subscribe' hallucinations, API returns segments only (no word times), CLI word mode corrupts Devanagari bytes, CPU-only here (Metal init failed) about 2x slower than realtime. Not adopted. Same-class engine as hyperframes transcribe.

forced_alignment.purpose: exact word boundaries inside continuous speech

ocr.purpose: find numbers/text on screen in b-roll (e.g. the cart total that matches a spoken price)
ocr.use_first: none yet; today: look at contact sheets

clip_search.purpose: 'find the moment that shows X' in b-roll

matting.status: engine tool present, untested on this footage

beats.purpose: beat / downbeat / drum-entrance of the music
beats.use_first: hyperframes beats (engine), then scripts/bgm_analyze.py to read band onsets
beats.status: engine tool not yet compared with bgm_analyze.py

stems.purpose: remove vocals so any song is a clean bed

loudness.use_first: ffmpeg loudnorm (single pass) in scripts/cut_master.py; ebur128 in scripts/build_audio.py

sfx.purpose: soft word-accent sounds only (no transition whooshes)
sfx.use_first: scripts/prep_sfx.py (local Kenney CC0 + Sonniss library, ~/hyperframes-assets/sfx) or the user's picks from videos/hyrox-creator-reel/sfx-sampler
sfx.status: works; no way to judge by ear, user picks from a numbered sampler

render.use_first: npx hyperframes@0.8.113 render -o exports/<name>.mp4 (run it as the background command itself)

qa.purpose: objective checks before the user sees a cut
qa.use_first: hyperframes check; video-critique (--allow-edge for full-bleed footage); quality-gate run_gate.sh; frame strips at every special moment
